newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes scarce, Latam activity brisk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes scarce, Latam activity brisk.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes remained scarce Thursday as refiners continued to focus on less pricey domestic grades, while Latin American spot activity was brisk, trade sources said.
The spread between January West Texas Intermediate and North Sea Brent was pegged at $1.05-1.15 a barrel, steady with Wednesday.
The WTI/Brent arbitrage has widened in recent days, but still falls short of the level required to make trans-Atlantic barrels economic into the U.S. Gulf Coast.
"The arb is closed for December. It's looking better for January, but not much better," one trader said.
Another trader noted that strong demand in Europe is keeping the barrels close to home.
Workers at three French refineries belonging to Elf Aquitaine are still on strike over proposed job cuts after eight days.
One Wall Street trader is thought to be holding four Brent cargoes in anticipation of working a VLCC trans-Atlantic.
In Latin America, Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) bought 400,000 barrels of Ecuadoran Oriente crude for January 14-17, trade sources said.
Tripetrol sold the cargo to ENAP for February WTI minus $3.75-4.00 a barrel fob, the sources said.
Oriente was sold to ENAP in November for Jan WTI minus $4.25 a barrel.
ENAP usually also buys West African crude such as Nigerian Escravos in its regular purchase tenders for 960,000 barrels, but offers were scarce in a tight market, traders said.
ENAP might issue another purchase tender next week for 960,000 barrels to retest the market, an ENAP official said.
Elsewhere, Shell is offering a cargo of Colombian Cano Limon for mid-January, asking Feb WTI minus $1.35 a barrel fob, traders said.
Separately, France's Total is offering a cargo of Colombian Cusiana for January 7-11, asking around Feb WTI plus 50 cents, traders said.
Colombia state oil company Ecopetrol is also offering South Blend for around January 20-22, trade sources said.
Meanwhile, bids are due today for 300,000 barrels of reconstituted crude on offer by Bolivian state oil company Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB).
Delivery is slated for December 25-30.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a series of partial January Brent cargoes traded at $24.66, $24.70 and $24.72, two to eight cents over the IPE settlement.
Intermonth spreads were weaker, with January/February Brent changing hands at 76 cents, down nine cents from the IPE close.
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
